# Goldfib Capital

> Goldfib Capital is a student-led research desk that delivers investment theses, institutional-grade equity research on Indian markets, and research automation to family offices at a fraction of the cost of an in-house team. Contact: partners@goldfibcapital.in

## Institutional Research, Decoded

- [Stock Lending in India: How SLB Lets You Earn on Shares You Already Own](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/securities-lending-borrowing-india/): Stock lending lets a shareholder lend shares to a borrower, usually a short seller or arbitrageur, for a fee. In India it happens through the exchange-run Securities Lending and Borrowing (SLB) segment on NSE and BSE, where the clearing corporation guarantees return of the shares. Lenders typically earn a fee equal to a small annualised percentage, higher for scarce stocks and around dividend or corporate action dates.
- [DCF Valuation for Indian Companies: Cost of Equity, Country Risk and the Terminal Value Trap](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/dcf-valuation-indian-companies/): A DCF for an Indian company should use rupee cash flows with a rupee discount rate. Build cost of equity from the government bond yield, a mature-market equity premium and a country risk premium, taking care not to double-count sovereign risk. Keep terminal growth below long-run nominal GDP growth. Always show a sensitivity table, because the terminal value usually drives most of the answer.
- [How to Analyse Indian Earnings Call Transcripts at Scale](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/earnings-call-transcript-analysis-india/): Treat each earnings call as one data point in a series, not as a standalone event. Extract every quantitative guidance statement into a tracker, score delivery against it each quarter, and flag changes in tone, topic and the share of evasive answers. AI can do the extraction across hundreds of transcripts in minutes, but analysts must verify every number and judge what it means.
- [Promoter Pledges and Shareholding Patterns: India's Most Underused Research Signal](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/promoter-pledging-shareholding-signals/): Promoter pledging means the promoter has used their shares as collateral for a loan. A high or rising pledge share is a risk because a falling share price can trigger margin calls and forced selling, which pushes the price down further. Read pledges together with promoter holding trends, institutional flows and insider trades. Combined, they are one of the strongest free signals in Indian equities.
- [How to Read an Indian Annual Report Like a Buy-Side Analyst](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/reading-indian-annual-report-checklist/): Don't start at the chairman's letter. Start with the auditor's report and CARO annexure, then the notes on related-party transactions, contingent liabilities and borrowings, then the cash flow statement, and only then the management discussion. That order puts the hardest-to-fake evidence first and the marketing last. It takes about 90 minutes.
- [The Coverage Gap: Why Most Listed Indian Companies Have No Analyst Watching](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/coverage-gap-indian-small-caps/): Most of India's several thousand listed companies get little or no sell-side coverage, because broker research is paid for by trading commissions and institutional interest, both of which concentrate in the largest few hundred stocks. Uncovered companies are priced on less information. That gap produces mispricing in both directions, so investors who do primary research there can find an edge.
- [What Makes Equity Research “Institutional-Grade”? A 12-Point Standard for Indian Markets](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/institutional-grade-equity-research-india/): Institutional-grade equity research is work a professional investor can act on without redoing it. It has a falsifiable thesis, a variant view versus consensus, a model tied to primary filings, explicit risks with triggers, a valuation range rather than a single number, and a documented review trail. Length and jargon are not the test; decision-usefulness is.

## Research Automation

- [Building Stock Screens for Indian Markets: From Factor Ideas to a Shortlist Worth Researching](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/stock-screening-india-factor-models/): A good stock screen for Indian markets narrows the listed universe to a shortlist worth researching, not to a buy list. Apply liquidity and size filters first, then quality factors (ROCE, cash conversion, leverage), governance filters (pledges, related-party transactions, auditor history), and finally value or momentum to rank what's left. Check for survivorship and look-ahead bias before trusting any backtest.
- [What a Research Desk Really Costs in India (and the Leaner Alternatives)](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/research-desk-cost-india/): An in-house equity research desk costs far more than analyst salaries. Add data and tool licences, recruitment and attrition, office overheads and the senior time spent reviewing work, and a two-analyst desk in India can cost several times the base payroll. Divide that by the number of finished reports and the cost per report is often much higher than teams expect. Calculate it before deciding to build, outsource or blend.
- [Building a Research Data Pipeline from NSE and BSE Filings](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/nse-bse-filings-research-data-pipeline/): A research data pipeline for Indian equities collects exchange filings (results, annual reports, shareholding patterns, transcripts and announcements) on a schedule. It stores the raw documents unchanged, extracts structured data into a database with source references, verifies material figures, and feeds models, screens and alerts. Use licensed vendors or official exchange channels for data, and follow each source's terms of use.
- [Automating Investment Research: What AI Can (and Can't) Do for an Indian Research Desk](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/ai-investment-research-automation-india/): AI and automation can take over most of the collection, extraction and first-draft work in equity research: pulling filings, extracting tables, summarising transcripts, updating models and flagging changes. They cannot yet be trusted with judgement: forming a variant view, weighing governance risk, or signing off numbers. The best results come from automating the pipeline end to end and putting a human checkpoint at every point where a number enters a decision.

## Family Office Playbook

- [Accredited Investors in India: Who Qualifies and What It Unlocks](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/accredited-investor-india/): India's equivalent of a US qualified investor is the SEBI accredited investor. Individuals and HUFs qualify with annual income of at least ₹2 crore, or net worth of at least ₹7.5 crore with ₹3.75 crore in financial assets, or ₹1 crore income plus ₹5 crore net worth. Accreditation, issued by KRA subsidiaries for up to three years, can unlock lower minimum tickets in AIFs and PMS and access to accredited-investor-only schemes.
- [Pre-IPO and Unlisted Shares in India: A Due Diligence Framework](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/pre-ipo-unlisted-shares-due-diligence-india/): Pre-IPO and unlisted shares can offer early access to growing companies, but they carry risks listed shares don't: thin information, wide bid-ask spreads, opaque pricing, lock-ins after listing and uncertain exits. Diligence should cover the company, the share's legal transferability, the price relative to recent funding rounds and listed peers, the realistic exit path, and the tax treatment of unlisted holdings.
- [PMS vs AIF vs Direct Equity: A Fee-Drag and Control Analysis for Indian HNIs](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/pms-vs-aif-vs-direct-equity-india/): PMS (minimum ₹50 lakh) holds stocks in your own demat account with a manager deciding trades. AIFs (generally a ₹1 crore minimum) pool money in a fund. Direct equity means you or your research team pick and hold stocks yourselves. Fees compound: a 2% fixed fee plus a 20% performance fee can cost a significant share of terminal wealth over ten years, so the manager's edge must clearly exceed it.
- [The Investment Memo Template Family Office Committees Actually Read](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/investment-memo-template-family-office/): A good investment memo fits the decision on page one: what we propose, why now, the variant view, the valuation range, the three biggest risks with triggers, position size and exit conditions. Supporting analysis follows as appendices. Add a pre-mortem (imagine it failed, then explain why) and a scored rubric so the committee judges every proposal on the same basis.
- [How Indian Family Offices Should Organise Their Research Function](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/family-office-research-function-india/): An Indian family office should keep three things in-house: the investment policy, the final decision, and one person who owns the thesis on each major position. Research volume can be bought or automated: screening, company initiations, monitoring, diligence support and data. A written operating rhythm (weekly monitoring, monthly pipeline review, quarterly portfolio review) matters more than headcount.

## Investor Tax & Accounts

- [How to Transfer Shares Between Demat Accounts in India (the ACAT Equivalent)](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/demat-account-transfer-india/): To move shares between demat accounts in India, you instruct the source depository participant through a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) or online through CDSL Easiest or NSDL SPEED-e. Transfers between your own accounts are in-kind: shares move without being sold, so no capital gains arise and your original cost and holding period carry over. Transfers usually settle in one to three working days.
- [AIS, Form 26AS and Capital Gains Statements: India's Answer to the K-1 Tax Document](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/ais-form-26as-capital-gains-india/): Indian investors have no single K-1 style document. Instead, three sources must agree: Form 26AS (tax deducted and paid against your PAN), the Annual Information Statement or AIS (everything reported about you, including share sales, dividends and interest), and your broker or mutual fund capital gains statement (cost, holding period and gain per lot). Reconcile them, fix mismatches through AIS feedback, then file your ITR.
- [ESOP Taxation in India: How Equity Compensation Is Taxed at Exercise and Sale](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/esop-taxation-india/): In India, ESOPs are taxed twice. At exercise, the gap between the share's fair market value and your exercise price is a perquisite, taxed as salary at your slab rate with TDS by the employer. At sale, the gain over that fair market value is a capital gain. For listed shares held over 12 months it is long-term and taxed at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh; otherwise short-term at 20%. Unlisted shares need 24 months for long-term treatment.

## Markets & Macro, Explained

- [What Is a Bear Market? India's Biggest Sensex Drawdowns and How Long Recovery Took](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/bear-market-india/): A bear market is a fall of 20% or more from a recent peak in a broad index, usually alongside pessimism and weak earnings. India has had several: the 1992 Harshad Mehta crash, the 2000 dot-com bust, the 2008 global financial crisis (Sensex down about 60%) and the 2020 Covid crash (about 38%). Recovery time ranged from under a year in 2020 to several years after 1992 and 2008.
- [What Is Inflation and CPI? How India Measures Prices and Why It Moves Your Portfolio](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/what-is-inflation-cpi-india/): Inflation is the rate at which the general price level rises, reducing what money can buy. In India it is measured mainly by the Consumer Price Index (CPI), published monthly by MoSPI around the 12th. Food is the largest component. The RBI targets 4% CPI inflation with a tolerance band of 2% to 6%, and sets the repo rate partly to keep inflation inside that band.
- [What Is GDP? Meaning, How India Measures It, and Why the Market Doesn't Track It](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/what-is-gdp-india/): GDP, or Gross Domestic Product, is the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a period. India's GDP is published quarterly by the National Statistics Office (MoSPI), about two months after each quarter ends. Real GDP removes inflation and measures volume growth; nominal GDP includes it. Nominal GDP matters for company revenues, and real GDP for economic growth.
- [What Is a Recession? Definition, Indian History and What It Means for Your Portfolio](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/what-is-a-recession-india/): A recession is a broad, sustained fall in economic activity: output, income, jobs and spending decline together. A common shorthand is two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP, called a technical recession. India has had full-year GDP contractions only four times since independence, most recently in 2020–21 (−5.8%) during the pandemic. More often India sees growth slowdowns, where GDP still grows but well below trend.

## The Student Research Model

- [The Equity Research Skills That Make a Student Analyst Useful on Day One](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/equity-research-skills-students-india/): A student becomes useful in equity research on day one by being able to read an annual report and its notes, build a driver-based three-statement model that reconciles to filings, write a clear one-page thesis, and source every number. Next come valuation, Python or spreadsheet automation, and presentation. Certifications help, but a portfolio of real, reviewed research work is the strongest signal.
- [Student-Led Equity Research: How the Model Works and Where It Beats Traditional Outsourcing](https://goldfibcapital.in/blog/student-led-equity-research-model/): A student-led research desk staffs research with strong finance and engineering students from top universities, supervised by experienced reviewers and supported by automation. Students bring time, effort and recent training. Process provides the quality: fixed templates, model audits and senior sign-off. The result is tailored, institutional-standard research at a fraction of the cost of an in-house desk, best suited to theses, initiations, screens and diligence support.
